statement: Agents should be able to send messages directly to one specific recipient.
Agents should be able to send messages to a chosen group of agents.
Agents should be able to broadcast messages to all available agents on the local network.
Agents should be able to join and leave groups dynamically.
The sender should be able to mark a message as protected when it contains sensitive content.
Unprotected messages can be handled normally.
Protected messages shall be secured primarily through encryption in transit.
Protected messages shall be restricted so that only intended recipients or authorized group members can access them.
Protected messages shall remain protected end to end.
Protected messages shall not be exposed in plain form to intermediate components.
Protected messages shall not be exposed in plain form to logs.
Protected messages shall not be exposed in plain form to any non-authorized agent.
The system should use a standard and widely accepted encryption algorithm rather than a custom scheme.
The encryption approach should be compatible with existing agentMom and legacy-agent setups.
If there is no existing standard in place, the system should use whatever the team considers current best practice for secure messaging.
The framework shall identify developers as key stakeholders who build on the framework.
The framework shall identify agents or applications as key stakeholders that use the framework.
The framework shall identify administrators or operators as key stakeholders who manage deployments and network communication behavior.
The framework shall support agents as a core object.
The framework shall support communication groups as a core object.
The framework shall support group memberships as a core object.
The framework shall support messages as a core object.
The framework shall support a protection or security setting attached to messages.
The framework may need conversation or delivery records for tracking.
The system shall provide some level of delivery status tracking, at least for direct and group messages.
For direct messages, the system shall indicate whether the recipient received the message.
For group messages, the system shall provide confirmation that the message was delivered to group members or accepted for delivery.
For broadcast messages, the system shall provide best-effort status information.
For protected messages, the system shall provide delivery traceability without exposing message content.
Agents should have a verified identity when participating in protected messaging or joining controlled groups.
The system should know who is allowed to receive what.
The framework should prefer mutual authentication for trusted agent-to-agent communication.
Anonymous communication should not be the default.
If anonymous communication is supported, it should be limited to very basic unprotected interactions.
The audit logs shall capture message sent events.
The audit logs shall capture message delivered events.
The audit logs shall capture message failed events.
The audit logs shall capture group joined events.
The audit logs shall capture group left events.
The audit logs shall capture authentication success or failure events.
The audit logs shall capture security-related changes such as enabling protection or changing membership rules.
For protected communication, the audit logs shall record that something was sent or received and who it involved.
If message titles, metadata, or identifiers could reveal too much, the audit logs shall redact or minimize them.
The system shall extend agentMom to support more flexible agent communication.
The system shall support targeted messaging between agents.
The system shall fit into the existing environment.
The framework shall not break existing applications.
The system shall support direct messages.
The system shall allow agents to join or leave groups dynamically.
The system shall provide a way to mark messages as protected when needed.
Any additional features shall be verified with the development team before commitment.
The system should provide some form of acknowledgment or delivery status.
The system may not need full reliability tracking for every broadcast.
The system shall provide a standard way for agents in multi-agent applications to communicate with each other.
The system shall fit into the existing agentMom environment.
The main users shall be software teams and platform groups that are building coordinated AI or agent-based workflows.
The system shall enable users to reuse the same communication patterns across different projects instead of building custom messaging each time.
The system shall make agent collaboration more reliable.
The system shall make agent collaboration easier to manage at scale.
An agent shall be able to send a direct task request to another agent.
The system shall support group conversations among agents working on the same job to share state.
The system shall support broadcast-style messages for system alerts and coordination signals that need to reach all agents on a local network.
An agent shall be defined as an autonomous software participant that can send and receive messages and take action on them.
Message protection shall require messages to be secured in transit and readable only by the intended recipients.
The system shall support broadcasts triggered by system-wide changes.
If an agent tries to send a message to a group that it is no longer part of, the system shall reject the message or return a clear error indicating that the agent is not an active member.
The system shall provide enough logging or status feedback to help teams diagnose whether a failure was caused by a membership issue, a network problem, or another cause.
If an agent tries to join a group that does not exist, the framework shall fail fast and return a clear error.
If an agent tries to join a group that does not exist, the framework shall allow the caller to create the group first or choose a different group.
If an agent leaves unexpectedly during an active conversation, the system shall remove the agent from the membership list immediately.
The framework shall enforce policy controls around group membership and protected messages.
Certain groups may be restricted so that only approved agents can join.
Protected messages shall be required whenever the content is sensitive.
Broadcasts shall be limited or filtered so they do not overwhelm the network.
The exact broadcast thresholds shall be set by the deployment team.
The framework may need to meet compliance expectations depending on the deployment location.
The framework should account for protected messages carrying sensitive business data.
The framework does not currently have a single mandated standard built into it.
The framework should support the encryption required by the hosting environment.
The framework should support the access control required by the hosting environment.
The framework should support the audit logging required by the hosting environment.
The framework shall be flexible rather than hard-coding one security model.
The framework shall support encrypted message transport.
The framework shall allow group membership to be enforced by policy or configuration.
The framework shall allow send permissions to be enforced by policy or configuration.
The framework shall produce logs for joins.
The framework shall produce logs for leaves.
The framework shall produce logs for sends.
The framework shall produce logs for failures.
The framework shall produce logs for protected message events.
Teams shall be able to plug in their own security providers.
Teams shall be able to plug in their own logging backends.
The framework shall allow teams to meet local requirements without changing the agent code.
Protected messages shall only be readable by agents that are authorized at the time the message is delivered.
If an agent leaves or loses permission, it shall stop seeing protected messages immediately.
Any cached or stored copies of protected messages shall be handled according to the deployment’s policy.
The framework shall avoid exposing sensitive content in logs, errors, or status messages unless explicitly configured to do so.
The framework shall send a membership-changed notification to the remaining participants when membership changes.
If the departing agent was the sender or was expected to respond, the other participants shall receive a clear timeout or unavailable signal instead of waiting indefinitely.
The application shall be able to re-route the conversation for recovery after a membership change.
The application shall be able to reassign the task for recovery after a membership change.
The application shall be able to reopen the group with the updated membership without losing the rest of the exchange.
The system shall expose notifications and recovery information as events or callbacks so applications can react to state changes.
The system shall not require applications to use polling to detect state changes.
The system shall provide a member joined event.
The system shall provide a member left event.
The system shall provide a group unavailable event.
The system shall provide a message delivery failed event.
The system shall provide a protected message access denied event.
The application shall be able to attach handlers to update its own conversation state.
The system shall provide an API for querying current membership.
The system shall provide an API for retrying a message.
The system shall provide an API for rerouting a message.

If an agent that drops out or is removed had pending work, the framework shall surface a failure or timeout event so the application can decide whether to retry, reassign, or continue without that participant.
Learnability shall be very important for the framework.
The framework should support teams that are adopting it to add communication into systems they already have.
The framework's tools, documentation, and examples shall work well with screen readers and keyboard-only workflows.
The framework should handle at least dozens of agents per local network in normal use.
The framework should define a practical upper limit for simultaneous conversations.
The framework should define a practical upper limit for message throughput.
The framework should avoid treating all agents and groups as one flat broadcast space.
The framework should support sharding by network segment or conversation domain to keep traffic local.
Membership updates should be event-driven and lightweight.
The system should account for network chatter as a main constraint.
The system should account for memory used for conversation state as a main constraint.
The system should account for the amount of history or membership tracking retained per group as a main constraint.
Routing shall use the updated membership information to decide which recipients should receive later messages.
If a member disappears unexpectedly, the system shall notify only the affected groups.
The system shall provide conversion support for any stored conversation or membership data from the old environment, if such data exists.
The system shall support a phased migration.
The system shall support mixed-version interoperability during a phased migration.
The system shall keep message formats stable enough for old and new agents to understand each other.
The system shall provide monitoring to detect routing or membership issues caused by a new module.
The system shall provide rollback paths if a new module causes routing or membership issues.
Hierarchical groups shall behave like nested scopes.
Recovery handling shall operate alongside routing as a fallback path.
Recovery handling shall support re-resolving group membership.
Recovery handling shall support switching to a safer delivery mode when a route appears stale.
Separating the modules shall keep each module simpler.
The system shall allow scalability by preventing membership churn from blocking message delivery everywhere at once.
If someone leaves unexpectedly, recovery shall clean up any queued deliveries or stale references.
Teams building agent-based applications currently solve communication in many different ways.
The system shall provide a reusable framework for agents to communicate reliably within a local network.
The system shall support agents coordinating in groups.
The system shall support managing protected messages without each project reinventing the underlying communication infrastructure.
Developers shall be able to plug the framework into existing agentMom-based applications and use it for normal day-to-day agent coordination with less custom code.
Agents shall be able to connect.
Agents shall be able to send messages to a specific agent or to a broader audience.
Agents shall be able to communicate predictably with the appropriate level of message protection when needed.
The communication framework shall typically be built by the platform or framework development team maintaining agentMom itself.
For a specific application, application developers or solution engineers shall configure which agents can communicate.
Human developers shall mostly interact with the communication framework when setting it up or troubleshooting the communication behavior.
A recipient shall mean one specific agent or endpoint that a message is intended for.
Protected messages shall require extra handling so that their contents are not exposed or altered in transit.
A message shall include the sender identity.
A message shall include the intended recipient identity.
A message shall include the actual content.
A message shall include a message type or purpose so the receiver knows how to handle it.
A message shall include an identifier so it can be tracked.
If protection is involved, the message structure shall indicate that status.
If protection is involved, the message structure shall include the metadata needed to process the message correctly.
The communication framework shall be fast enough for agents to coordinate in near real time for ordinary workflow tasks.
The communication framework shall provide dependable delivery within the local network.
If a message cannot be delivered, the framework shall make the delivery failure visible rather than failing silently.
For protected messages, the additional handling shall not slow down normal use too much.
A conversation shall start when one agent initiates a message to another agent or to a group.
An agent shall join a group to participate in a shared activity.
Existing agentMom applications shall keep running without major rewrites.
The system shall be built so that new communication patterns can be added in a modular way.
The system shall allow developers to plug in new message handling or routing logic.
The framework shall use a safe default rather than guessing when handling an unrecognized message type or delivery path.
When a message type or delivery path is not recognized, the framework shall either route it through the most conservative supported path or reject it clearly with an explanation.
If protection is involved, the framework shall not automatically downgrade security just to make delivery happen.
The expanded communication framework shall be lightweight enough for agents to run without heavy infrastructure.
The expanded communication framework shall not require manual administration.
The expanded communication framework shall tolerate mixed environments in which some applications are older agentMom-based systems and others use the expanded framework.
The expanded communication framework shall avoid introducing a lot of operational overhead.
Configuration should preferably default to the existing behavior unless someone explicitly enables the new communication features.
The framework shall isolate newer capabilities so older applications are not forced to understand them or be configured for them.
The framework shall not depend on any external cloud service for the core communication path.
A typical deployment shall support tens of agents.
A typical deployment shall support a handful of groups active at once.
The system is not expected to support hundreds or thousands of agents or groups in a typical deployment.
The system should ideally be able to scale beyond the typical deployment size.
The system shall fail closed for protected messages if it cannot confirm a valid delivery path.
The system shall not silently reroute protected content through an unverified fallback.
The system shall surface a clear delivery error quickly so the sender knows the message did not go through.
If the system retries delivery, it shall retry only through another path that is equally trusted and explicitly supported.
For one-to-one communication, the sender field shall be mandatory.
A response correlation field shall be optional in general.
A response correlation field shall be required when the sender expects a reply or needs to match the response to the original message.
The framework should respect the membership and authorization rules in place for the relevant context.
An agent should be excluded from receiving a protected message if it has not been cleared to handle that message type or protection level, even if it is technically in the group.
Agents that are offline, not fully joined, or not authorized for the specific communication can be excluded from receiving the message.
The framework shall use a short retry window with a bounded number of retry attempts.
The retry policy shall not stall the conversation for an extended period.
After the retry window is exhausted, the framework shall notify the sender.
The retry timing shall be set based on the expected local network behavior.
There may be organizational restrictions on how messages are handled in the agentMom environment, especially for protected messages and audit logs.
The framework should minimize retention by default.
The framework should avoid logging message contents unless logging is explicitly allowed.
A protected one-to-one message envelope shall include the protection type or mode.
A protected one-to-one message envelope shall include whatever key, reference, or token is needed for the receiver to unwrap or validate the message.
A protected one-to-one message envelope shall include any integrity or authenticity metadata such as a signature or checksum, if such metadata is present.
A retry on an alternative path shall be allowed only if the protection requirements can still be preserved end to end.
Rerouting shall be allowed for transport problems.
The placement of a policy label should be determined by who needs to act on the label.
If intermediaries need a policy label for routing, filtering, or enforcement, the label has to stay in the envelope in a visible form.
If only the receiver needs a policy label, the label can be embedded in the protected payload.
There may be cases where policy must be visible to network controls even though the content remains hidden.
For near-real-time coordination, the framework should treat delays of more than a few seconds as problematic.
The framework may be slower for background tasks.
The framework may be slower for bulk group broadcasts.
The framework may be slower for anything that is explicitly not time-sensitive.
The exact delay threshold for problematic near-real-time coordination must be agreed based on the target use cases.
The system may keep low-priority or non-urgent messages queued longer if it is explicitly configured to do so.
The system shall determine additional queueing for low-priority or non-urgent messages based on message priority.
The system shall determine additional queueing for low-priority or non-urgent messages based on sender policy.
The system shall determine additional queueing for low-priority or non-urgent messages based on the recipient group’s retention rules, if such rules exist.
The system shall enforce a firm maximum duration for additional queueing so that the queue does not grow without bound.
The system shall make the additional queueing duration short and configurable.
Advanced routing and policy behaviors may be deferred for the first release.
Features that depend on complex network-wide discovery or automatic optimization may be deferred for the first release.
The first version shall focus on reliable one-to-one communication.
The first version shall focus on reliable group communication.
The first version shall provide basic protection choices.
Smarter rerouting may be deferred until later.
Richer policy negotiation may be deferred until later.
The first release shall be tolerant of older applications that only use a subset of the expected behavior.
The system shall ensure that the core message can still be understood and delivered safely.
The system shall enforce hard limits based on security level, recipient scope, and message criticality before altering the default delivery path.
The framework shall not reroute the message at all when it is still too sensitive, the recipient set is too broad, or the message is too critical to reroute safely.
